name: Websites
summary: A focused site that explains the offer and makes the next step easy to find.
metaDescription: Plan and build a business website with clear content, responsive design, accessible pages, useful forms and the next step in view.
promise: Give your offer a useful place to land.
intro: A business website should help the right people understand what you do, see why it matters and take a useful next step.
audience: Your offer has changed, but the site still describes an earlier version of the business.
Visitors reach the site but cannot quickly find the right service or next step.
A launch, new market or new product needs a clear digital home.
Several pages, forms and content updates need one consistent structure.
deliverables: Key messages and calls to action

process.name: Discover
process.description: Review the offer, audience, existing content and the decisions the site should support.

process.name: Define
process.description: Set page priorities, navigation, key messages and the path from entry to enquiry.
process.deliverable: A page map and content outline

process.name: Design
process.description: Shape the page hierarchy, visual direction and responsive states before development.

process.name: Build
process.description: Implement the pages, interactions, forms and agreed content tools.

process.name: Test
process.description: Check content, keyboard use, mobile layouts, forms, metadata and image loading.

process.name: Launch
process.description: Publish the approved site and hand over the files and operating notes.

useCases: A service business needs to explain several offers without sending visitors through a long menu.
A new product needs a launch site with a clear route to enquiry or signup.
An established site needs a new structure that reflects current services and content.

faqs.question: Can ZEC work with our current content system?
faqs.answer: Yes. The project can extend a suitable existing system or use a simpler publishing setup when that better fits the team and content.

faqs.question: Can an existing website be redesigned?
faqs.answer: Yes. The work can start with the current site, identify what should stay and replace the parts that no longer support the offer or user journey.

faqs.question: How long does a website take?
faqs.answer: Timing depends on page count, content readiness, integrations and review cycles. A project schedule is set after the scope is agreed.

faqs.question: What does a website project cost?
faqs.answer: Cost follows the agreed pages, functionality and content needs. ZEC provides a scoped estimate before work begins.

name: Web applications
summary: A browser-based product for workflows, accounts, data and repeat tasks.
metaDescription: Design and build a web application around defined workflows, user roles, data and integrations, from early scope through release.
promise: Give complex work a better interface.
intro: A web application brings a defined workflow into one place, with the right views, permissions and actions for each user.
audience: A recurring task depends on spreadsheets, email and manual handoffs.
Customers or staff need a secure way to view or update information.
A dashboard must make operational data easier to understand and act on.
A product concept needs a usable first release in the browser.
deliverables: Core user journeys and interface states

process.name: Discover
process.description: Map the users, current workflow, data sources and points where work slows down.

process.name: Define
process.description: Choose the first workflows, roles, permissions and boundaries for the release.

process.name: Design
process.description: Design navigation, screens, forms and system feedback for each important state.

process.name: Build
process.description: Implement the interface and connect it to the agreed data and service layer.

process.name: Test
process.description: Exercise user roles, data states, keyboard paths, device sizes and failure cases.

process.name: Launch
process.description: Release the agreed scope, document the key flows and set out the next decisions.

useCases: A team needs one dashboard for tasks that currently move between separate spreadsheets.
Customers need a portal to check status, submit information or manage an account.
A service operation needs role-specific screens around an existing data source.

faqs.question: Can ZEC design a dashboard or customer portal?
faqs.answer: Yes. The scope can include dashboards, account areas, internal tools and customer-facing portals around a defined workflow.

faqs.question: Can a web app connect to systems we already use?
faqs.answer: Potentially. The available API, permissions and data quality are reviewed before the integration approach is agreed.

faqs.question: How are user roles handled?
faqs.answer: Roles and access rules are defined early, then reflected in the interface and implementation requirements.

faqs.question: How long does an application take?
faqs.answer: The schedule depends on the number of workflows, data sources, roles and review needs. Timing is confirmed after scoping.

name: Digital platforms
summary: A connected service for multiple audiences, roles or parts of an operation.
metaDescription: Connect multiple audiences, roles and workflows in a digital platform, with a clear first scope and room for essential services.
intro: A digital platform coordinates a wider service: different users, connected workflows and information that needs to move between them.
audience: A service involves more than one audience, role or organization.
Information is spread across disconnected tools or service touchpoints.
A directory, marketplace or member service needs a consistent structure.
A platform needs to support a new workflow without losing sight of its users.

process.name: Discover
process.description: Understand the participants, service model, current tools and dependencies.

process.name: Define
process.description: Set the first audience groups, permissions, shared records and release boundary.

process.name: Design
process.description: Connect the journeys and create a consistent system for different roles.

process.name: Build
process.description: Implement the agreed journeys and connect the services that need to share data.

process.name: Test
process.description: Review each role, key data exchange, permission boundary and fallback state.

process.name: Launch
process.description: Release the agreed service, hand over operating notes and prioritize the next phase.

useCases: A membership service needs distinct spaces for members and administrators.
A directory needs to connect listings, search, enquiries and ownership updates.
A partner service needs a shared view of requests moving between organizations.

faqs.question: How is a platform different from a web application?
faqs.answer: A platform often connects several audiences or services. The structure is shaped around those relationships, shared data and permissions.

faqs.question: Can a platform be delivered in phases?
faqs.answer: Yes. The first release can focus on the most useful connected workflows, with later phases guided by use and operational needs.

faqs.question: Can existing systems be integrated?
faqs.answer: The options depend on the systems and their APIs. ZEC maps the integration requirements before committing to a technical approach.

faqs.question: What affects platform scope?
faqs.answer: Audience roles, data ownership, integrations, permissions and operational requirements all shape the scope.

name: E-commerce
summary: An online store that helps people discover, compare and purchase products.
metaDescription: Build an online store with a clear product structure and considered browsing, checkout, payment and fulfilment paths across devices.
promise: Make the path from product to purchase work.
intro: An online store should make the product range easy to understand and the purchase path reliable on the devices people use.
audience: Products are difficult to discover or compare in the current store.
The checkout, product information or mobile shopping flow creates friction.
A new product range needs a considered online storefront.
Catalogues, inventory or order handoffs need a more connected experience.
deliverables: Product listing and detail page designs
Product content and search metadata structure

process.name: Discover
process.description: Review the catalogue, shopper questions, fulfilment model and current purchase path.

process.name: Define
process.description: Set catalogue structure, product attributes, checkout needs and platform boundaries.

process.name: Design
process.description: Shape browsing, product comparison, cart and checkout for desktop and mobile.

process.name: Build
process.description: Implement the storefront and connect the agreed catalogue, payment and fulfilment services.

process.name: Test
process.description: Review product data, checkout states, mobile use, confirmation messages and integration paths.

process.name: Launch
process.description: Prepare the catalogue, publish the store and hand over order and content guidance.

useCases: A product range needs useful filters, comparison and clear product details.
A small catalogue needs a streamlined store and familiar checkout.
An existing store needs a more consistent mobile purchase journey.

faqs.question: Can ZEC improve an existing online store?
faqs.answer: Yes. The work can focus on product discovery, store structure, mobile use or specific steps in the purchase path.

faqs.question: Which store platform should we use?
faqs.answer: The choice depends on catalogue needs, operations, integrations and who will manage the store. It is part of the definition work.

faqs.question: Can payment and fulfilment tools be connected?
faqs.answer: Integration options depend on the chosen platform and service APIs. They are checked before the build scope is fixed.

faqs.question: How long does an e-commerce project take?
faqs.answer: The schedule depends on catalogue size, content readiness, integrations and review cycles. A timeline is agreed after scoping.

name: SaaS MVPs
summary: A focused first release for testing one product workflow with real users.
metaDescription: Shape a SaaS MVP around one product question, then design and build the core user workflow for a focused first release.
promise: Build the smallest useful product release.
intro: An MVP should focus on the product question that matters most, then make that core workflow usable enough to learn from.
audience: A product idea has more features than the first release can support.
A team needs a working prototype to evaluate a defined workflow.
A product concept needs a foundation for iterative development.
Stakeholders need to agree what belongs in the first version.

process.name: Discover
process.description: Understand the product idea, intended user and the assumption the first release should examine.

process.name: Define
process.description: Separate the core workflow from later features and set a practical release boundary.

process.name: Design
process.description: Prototype the key journey and resolve the interface decisions before implementation.

process.name: Build
process.description: Implement the agreed first workflow, account states and essential integrations.

process.name: Test
process.description: Review the core journey with realistic data and capture issues that block learning.
process.deliverable: A release review and feedback plan

process.name: Launch
process.description: Release to the intended audience and organize the next product decisions.
process.deliverable: A first release and prioritized backlog

useCases: A software idea needs one end-to-end workflow before a wider feature set is considered.
A service business wants to test a self-service product alongside its existing offer.
A team needs a prototype and scoped release to align product and development work.

faqs.question: What makes a product an MVP?
faqs.answer: It is the smallest release that supports a meaningful core workflow and the learning objective agreed during discovery.

faqs.question: Does an MVP include production-ready code?
faqs.answer: The build approach is agreed for the intended release. The work avoids adding unnecessary features while keeping the next steps visible.

faqs.question: Can ZEC help define what to leave out?
faqs.answer: Yes. Prioritization and release boundaries are part of the definition stage.

faqs.question: What happens after the first release?
faqs.answer: The team reviews use and feedback, then chooses the next improvements based on the product goals.

name: Custom systems
summary: A purpose-built business tool shaped around the operation it supports.
metaDescription: Plan a custom business system around real operations, team roles and handoffs, connecting approved data sources and existing tools.
promise: Fit the software to the way the work runs.
intro: When standard tools leave gaps between people and processes, a custom system can bring the relevant work into a more coherent flow.
audience: A team repeats the same administrative steps across several tools.
Existing software does not match the way the operation is organized.
Requests, approvals or records move through unclear handoffs.
Several tools need to share information without adding more manual work.
deliverables: Custom tool interface and implementation plan
Error handling and operational feedback states

process.name: Discover
process.description: Observe the workflow, handoffs, tools and exceptions that shape the operation.

process.name: Define
process.description: Set the system boundary, user roles, key records and what remains in existing tools.

process.name: Design
process.description: Prototype the operational screens and feedback for normal and exception paths.

process.name: Build
process.description: Implement the agreed tool and connect the approved data sources and services.

process.name: Test
process.description: Review permissions, edge cases, data handling and the steps people use each day.

process.name: Launch
process.description: Release the agreed workflows and hand over operating notes to the people using them.

useCases: A service operation needs one place to track requests from intake to completion.
A team needs a structured approval flow with clear ownership at each step.
A business needs a small tool that connects existing records with daily work.

faqs.question: When does a business need a custom system?
faqs.answer: It may fit when the workflow is specific, standard tools leave important gaps and the process is stable enough to define.

faqs.question: Can a custom system work with our existing software?
faqs.answer: Potentially. Existing APIs, data ownership and access rules are reviewed before integration work is proposed.

faqs.question: Can a system be built in stages?
faqs.answer: Yes. A first release can focus on one high-value workflow, with other parts added when they are ready to be defined.

faqs.question: How is the project scoped?
faqs.answer: Scope starts with the process, users, data and exceptions. ZEC then proposes an agreed release boundary and estimate.

name: AI & workflow automation
summary: Connected workflows that reduce repetitive handoffs and keep people in control.
metaDescription: Design workflow automation and bounded AI assistance around repetitive tasks, with clear checks, human review and fallback paths.
promise: Automate the repeat work. Keep judgment with people.
intro: Automation can move information between tools, while AI can assist with bounded tasks such as classification or drafting. Each flow needs clear checks and a human fallback.
audience: Staff copy the same information between forms, inboxes and business tools.
Routine intake, routing or status updates consume time every week.
A process needs an AI-assisted step with review before action is taken.
Existing integrations need monitoring, clear failure handling or better ownership.
deliverables: Workflow orchestration, including n8n-compatible patterns where suitable
Bounded AI prompts and structured outputs when appropriate

process.name: Discover
process.description: Map the repeat work, inputs, tools, people and cases that need judgment.

process.name: Define
process.description: Choose a bounded first flow and set privacy, review, fallback and success criteria.

process.name: Design
process.description: Specify triggers, routing, human checks, data fields and failure notifications.

process.name: Build
process.description: Connect the approved tools and implement deterministic steps plus any bounded AI assistance.

process.name: Test
process.description: Exercise expected, missing, malformed and failure inputs before the flow is relied on.
process.deliverable: Test cases and a monitored pilot

process.name: Launch
process.description: Release the agreed flow, document ownership and set the review process.

useCases: New enquiries can be categorized and routed, with a person reviewing uncertain cases.
A team can synchronize approved records between a form and its operations system.
Incoming documents can be summarized into a draft that a staff member checks before use.

faqs.question: What can workflow automation handle?
faqs.answer: It can move data, trigger routine actions and route work between connected tools. Each flow is scoped around its inputs, permissions and exceptions.

faqs.question: Where does AI fit in an automated workflow?
faqs.answer: AI can assist with bounded tasks such as classification or drafting. Output should be checked before important or irreversible actions.

faqs.question: Does every automation need AI?
faqs.answer: No. A predictable process is often better handled with clear rules and integrations. AI is included only where it fits the task.

faqs.question: Can ZEC work with n8n or our existing tools?
faqs.answer: The workflow can use n8n-style orchestration or another suitable tool. Existing APIs, data access and operating requirements shape the choice.
